clue.text: Italian girl showing cleavage in East

parts.note: Flo is a short form of the girl's name Florence
a rent is a split or tear, a cleaving
E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A girl from Italy is wearing a low-cut top somewhere out East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleavage' suggests a neckline, but here it means a split, RENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Florence is an Italian, so the city's adjective serves as a noun for one.

clue.text: Clue that's found in middle of drawer

definitions.text: that's found in middle of drawer

explanation.surface: A clue found in the middle drawer of a desk.
explanation.definitionFit: A clue is a hint for detectives; graphite sits in the middle of a pencil, which draws.

clue.text: Wind up? Retreat!

explanation.surface: Two commands: get ready, then fall back.
explanation.definitionFit: To coil again is to wind up; to spring back in fear is to shrink away.

clue.text: Is such an acquaintance agreeable?

parts.note: plays on a slight acquaintance known by a greeting gesture, and that gesture of the head signalling agreement

explanation.definitionFit: Bowing the head shows assent, and a slight friend is known only by such a greeting.

clue.text: One thing I met on the way up

indicators.note: in a down clue, on the way up says the word met reads from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Something I met while climbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way up' reverses MET to TEM.
explanation.definitionFit: An individual article in a list is a single object.

clue.text: Possibly see unit as part of another unit

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Perhaps viewing a flat as a part of a larger block.
explanation.definitionFit: A bathroom attached to a bedroom is part of that bedroom suite.

clue.text: Cheer pilot manoeuvring hovercraft

indicators.note: manoeuvring suggests moving pieces around, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Applaud the pilot steering a hovercraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A chopper is an aircraft that can hover in one place.

clue.text: Having reached Wembley, then failin',maybe!

indicators.note: maybe hints that the preceding letters are a possible rearrangement

explanation.surface: A team gets to Wembley, then perhaps loses.
explanation.walkthrough: Wembley Stadium in London hosts English cup finals.
explanation.definitionFit: Reaching Wembley means qualifying for the last match of a cup competition.

clue.text: Intend to get tight

explanation.surface: Planning to get drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: To intend something is to have it in mind; tight-fisted, stingy people are called this.

clue.text: Desire clothing but not the ordinary sort

definitions.text: Desire clothing but not the ordinary sort

parts.note: to fancy something is to desire it

explanation.surface: Someone longs for clothes that are out of the ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Costumes worn to a themed party are outfits deliberately unlike everyday wear.

clue.text: Highly bumptious?

parts.note: read as 'somewhat up', the word is 'up' with the suffix meaning 'rather' attached, while also meaning conceited

explanation.definitionFit: Self-important and pushy people behave in an arrogant, above-their-station way.

clue.text: Using a tool around a defect

indicators.note: around tells us the tool word goes outside the single letter

parts.note: filing is working with a file, a tool

explanation.surface: Someone works with a tool to fix a fault.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortcoming or weakness in character is a defect.

clue.text: Mistake that makes one late

parts.note: 'late' suggests unpunctuality but means deceased, so the blunder is a deadly one

explanation.definitionFit: A computing term for a crash-causing bug, read literally as a deadly slip.

clue.text: Never satisfied with played out banalities

indicators.note: played out signals the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Bored by stale clichés.
explanation.definitionFit: Greedy people whose appetite cannot be met are unsatisfiable.

clue.text: A girl in distress, the object of chivalrous attention

indicators.note: in distress suggests disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A damsel in distress draws a knight's chivalry.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface wants the damsel as the object of chivalry; it is the Holy cup sought by Arthur's knights.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthurian knights quested for the Holy cup.

clue.text: Break one's journey and don't go on

explanation.surface: Interrupt your trip and stay put.
explanation.definitionFit: Pausing a trip at an intermediate place is a halt en route; to cease and be off is the other sense.

clue.text: Handle the company's capital

explanation.surface: Managing a firm's money.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun or whip handle has this name; shares make up a firm's capital.

clue.text: Sound harsh or sound wonderful

indicators.note: the second sound tells us the word for wonderful is said aloud

explanation.surface: A noise can be grating or marvellous.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'sound' plays two roles: the first means 'make a noise', the second is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal scraping on metal gives a rasping, jarring noise.

clue.text: Imposed duty

parts.note: suggests a tax or levy, but means a job someone has been set

explanation.definitionFit: A piece of work assigned to someone is an obligation laid upon them.

clue.text: Heads turn in shock

indicators.note: turn tells us the slang word for heads is read backwards

explanation.surface: People's heads turn in surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: To daze or astonish someone is to shock them.

clue.text: You can put it on a horse that's a sure thing

definitions.text: You can put it on a horse

explanation.surface: Betting on a horse that is certain to win.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddle girth fastened round a horse has this name; a certainty is a dead cert.

clue.text: Char with mop out clears away moths

definitions.note: a verb phrase defining a noun: the substance that repels moths

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A cleaner with a mop drives out moths.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a char is a cleaning lady, which feeds the surface picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Mothballs were made of this aromatic substance, used as a moth repellent.

clue.text: Teacher confused by area of France

indicators.note: confused tells us the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A teacher bewildered by the geography of France.
explanation.definitionFit: A metric unit of land measure, devised in France, of ten thousand square metres.

clue.text: Sort of thinking of belonging to the side

explanation.surface: A type of thought that sits at the edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Creative, indirect problem solving is a well-known kind of thinking; sideways or flanking is the anatomical sense.

clue.text: Bird of prey, some of the quickest rely on surprise

indicators.note: some of tells us the answer is a part of the following words

explanation.surface: A hawk relies on speed and surprise to catch its quarry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some of' points to letters within 'quickest rely'.
explanation.definitionFit: This small falcon hovers before swooping on prey.

clue.text: It takes a good deal to satisfy him

definitions.text: It takes a good deal to satisfy him

parts.words: It takes a good deal to satisfy him
parts.note: 'a good deal' reads as 'a lot' but means a profitable bargain

explanation.definitionFit: A merchant is pleased by a profitable bargain.

clue.text: Way to the top — and why you can't get there?

explanation.surface: A route to the summit, and the reason it is blocked.
explanation.walkthrough: A sign reading this phrase in Britain warns of roadworks closing the route.
explanation.definitionFit: British signage for a street being dug up explains a blocked route.

clue.text: Elderly, but managed without a valet

indicators.note: without says the word for a valet is taken out

parts.note: a man is a manservant such as a valet

explanation.surface: An old person who coped without a servant.
explanation.definitionFit: Old people are advanced in years.

clue.text: Church and nest builder

explanation.surface: A builder of churches and of nests.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Christopher Wren designed St Paul's Cathedral and many London churches; 'builder' serves both.
explanation.definitionFit: The architect of many London churches; also a tiny bird that builds nests.

clue.text: Stranded on a peak without liquor

explanation.surface: Marooned on a mountain with nothing to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Left helpless like a beached boat; also literally elevated and alcohol-free.

clue.text: Capital I and endless loose change

indicators.note: change signals the remaining letters are rearranged
endless says the final letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: A capital I and some loose change lying about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' removes the final E of 'loose', leaving LOOS, which 'change' rearranges; 'I and' are linking words of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the capital city of Norway.

clue.text: It may put one off old Russian fish

parts.note: Red was a term for a Soviet-era Russian communist

explanation.surface: Old Russian fish might put you off your food.
explanation.definitionFit: A misleading clue that distracts is a false trail.
